newsitem.title: CHINA: HK people gloomy on rule of law under China - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK people gloomy on rule of law under China - poll.

text.p: Hong Kong people have taken a glum view about political conditions and the rule of law since China took over on July 1, a survey showed on Thursday.
Just 33 percent see political conditions improving.
Some 60 percent hold no view or think the situation is the same as when Britain ruled the roost, the Hong Kong University poll shows.
Hong Kong was transferred to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after 156 years under British colonial rule.

Some 21 percent of those polled said the rule of law had weakened since the handover, while only 5.8 percent thought it was stronger. Almost half of the respondents believed nothing at all had changed, the poll showed.
The poll found nearly 44 percent less confident in the rule of law after new leader Tung Chee-hwa froze labour rights laws last week.

The "rule of law" is a buzzword for stability in Hong Kong, a reference to the British-based Common Law legal system that has underpinned the runaway development of this society of 6.4 million people.
